Experience.title: Experience
Experience.content:
Experience
Epic Games — London, UK
ML Research Intern (Part-time) · Feb 2026 – Present
Improving the AI Assistant for Unreal Engine and its Code Generation Agent, where LLM agents struggle with tool use in domain-specific, low-resource programming environments. Finetuning and post-training code generation models; developing evaluation harnesses and feedback mechanisms; improving intent understanding and output accuracy for game development workflows.
Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab — London, UK
Research Intern, NLP · Feb 2025 – Sept 2025
Improved retrieval-augmented theorem autoformalization with LLMs, addressing under-specified retrieval queries and weak guidance on how to use retrieved premises. Built DRIFT, a retrieval-augmented autoformalization pipeline that decomposes queries and retrieves premises and illustrative examples with a finetuned BGE-M3 retriever. Delivered up to 13.3 F1 improvement on retrieval and 42.3% absolute improvement on downstream autoformalization (BEq+@10). Paper accepted to ICLR 2026.
Antobot — UK
Computer Vision Engineer · Oct 2018 – Sept 2021
Deployed robust fruit detection, tracking, and yield estimation on edge devices for autonomous field robotics. Delivered an end-to-end perception stack: curated instance-segmentation datasets, trained real-time detection and tracking models, and built regression modules for yield and fruit size estimation. Production-deployed on-device perception pipeline using TensorRT and ONNX on edge hardware.

Priaxis — Autonomous Personalised Agent System
2025 – Present

Approach: A multi-agent system built on the Claude Code SDK and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for structured tool use, with personalised planning and execution grounded in user history and preferences.

Publications.title: Publications
Publications.content:
ACL 2026



Failure Modes in Multi-Hop QA: The Weakest Link Effect and Recognition Bottleneck
Meiru Zhang, Zaiqiao Meng, Nigel Collier
ACL 2026

PDF


Abstract
Multi-hop QA fails in long contexts due to position bias. We propose Multi-Focus Attention Instruction (MFAI) and evaluate 5 LLMs on MuSiQue and NeoQA, identifying recognition failure as the main bottleneck and proposing the "Weakest Link Effect".





ICLR 2026



DRIFT: Decompose, Retrieve, Illustrate, then Formalize Theorems
Meiru Zhang, Philipp Borchert, Milan Gritta, Gerasimos Lampouras
International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR), 2026

PDF


Abstract
DRIFT is a retrieval-augmented autoformalization pipeline that decomposes queries, retrieves premises and illustrative examples, and achieves significant improvements over baselines on theorem formalization tasks.





ACL 2025



The Power of Simplicity in LLM-Based Event Forecasting
Meiru Zhang, Auss Abbood, Zaiqiao Meng, Nigel Collier
First Workshop for Research on Agent Language Models (REALM), ACL 2025

PDF


Abstract
We replace multi-step agentic reasoning (e.g., ReAct) with a single-step RAG pipeline and show that structured evidence beats raw headlines at ~10% of ReAct inference cost for event forecasting.





EMNLP 2024



Can We Instruct LLMs to Compensate for Position Bias?
Meiru Zhang, Zaiqiao Meng, Nigel Collier
Findings of EMNLP, 2024

PDF


Abstract
We propose Attention Instruction to steer LLM attention and improve controllability by reweighting attention to target prompt regions, compensating for position bias in in-context learning.





ACL 2023



COFFEE: A Contrastive Oracle-Free Framework for Event Extraction
Meiru Zhang, Yixuan Su, Zaiqiao Meng, Zihao Fu, Nigel Collier
First Workshop on Matching From Unstructured and Structured Data (MATCHING), ACL 2023

PDF


Abstract
We introduce the Oracle-Free Event Extraction (OFEE) setting and develop the COFFEE framework, enabling event extraction without oracle triggers and providing a stronger, more realistic evaluation protocol.





ICMI 2019



Multi-modal Active Learning From Human Data: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
Ognjen Rudovic, Meiru Zhang, Bjorn Schuller, Rosalind Picard
International Conference on Multimodal Interaction (ICMI), 2019

PDF


Abstract
We build multimodal user-state models and implement a DQN-based active learning agent to select the most informative samples for labeling, reducing annotation waste for multi-class classification.

blog/llm-position-bias-rag.title: LLM Position Bias and RAG Mechanism
blog/llm-position-bias-rag.content:
LLM Position Bias and RAG Mechanism
This post explores position bias in Large Language Models and its implications for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems.
What is Position Bias in LLMs?
Position bias refers to the tendency of LLMs to favor information presented at certain positions within the input context. Studies have shown that models often:

Give more weight to information at the beginning (primacy bias)
Sometimes favor information at the end (recency bias)
May overlook or underweight information in the middle

Position Bias in RAG Systems
Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines information retrieval with text generation. Position bias becomes critical because:

Retrieved documents are typically concatenated in the prompt
The order of these documents can significantly affect the model’s output
Important information buried in the middle may be ignored

Mitigation Strategies
1. Document Reranking

Strategically place most relevant documents at optimal positions
Consider both relevance score and position effects

2. Context Compression

Remove redundant information
Keep context concise to reduce position effects

3. Multiple Passes

Query the model multiple times with different document orderings
Aggregate results for more robust outputs

4. Instruction Engineering

Explicitly instruct models to consider all context equally
Use prompts that encourage comprehensive analysis

My research is driven by the potential of AI in real-world applications (“AI for good”). I am honoured to be part of the Gates Cambridge community.
